in_hindi.long_meaning: ख़लवात नाम का अर्थ है दुनिया से अलग होकर आत्म-खोज और आध्यात्मिक विकास की यात्रा। यह नाम अरबी मूल 'خلا' से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है खालीपन या एकांत। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, यह नाम आध्यात्मिक ज्ञान और आंतरिक शांति की खोज के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है।

in_pashto.name: خلوات
in_pashto.long_meaning: خلوات د نړۍ څخه د جلا کولو او د روحاني ودې او ځان پوهې د لارې چارې معنی لري. دا نوم د عربي ريښې 'خلا' څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چې د خالي ځای یا تنهایي معنی لري. د افغان او پښتن مسلمانو په دود، دا نوم د روحاني لارښوونې او داخلي سولې د لټون لپاره کارول کیږي.

in_english.name: Khalawat
in_english.meaning: Solitude; withdrawal from worldly life for spiritual growth
in_english.long_meaning: Khalawat is an Arabic name that signifies solitude or withdrawal from the worldly life to focus on spiritual growth and self-discovery. Etymologically derived from the Arabic root 'خلا' (khala), meaning 'to empty' or 'to withdraw', this name holds significant spiritual connotations in Islamic tradition. Historically, it has been used to describe states of deep contemplation and spiritual retreat, aligning with Sufi practices of introspection and devotion.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Khalawat" holds a significant place in various Islamic communities, particularly in the Sufi tradition. It is often used as a title for Sufis who are renowned for their deep devotion to God. These individuals are known for their intense spiritual practices, which may include long hours of meditation, recitation of the Quran, and acts of charity. They are considered spiritual guides and teachers, inspiring others to follow the path of God.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Khalawat" reflects the deep spiritual commitment and devotion to God that is at the heart of the Islamic faith. The term "khalawat" comes from the Arabic root word "khulwah," which means "solitude" or "seclusion." This is a reference to the spiritual practice of secluding oneself from the world in order to deepen one's connection with God. The name serves as a reminder that true spiritual growth often comes through dedication, focus, and a profound sense of devotion to the divine.
